The 45 codes are therefore not validated, and the paper's central empirical artifact is 'descriptive only'.

The coding is lopsided: 43 of 45 cells are 'documented', none are contradicted, and 37 of 43 cite a single source. The tags give little discrimination. Cases cannot be compared when almost every cell has the same value. The paper also admits that reference counts do not show independence.

Two documented cells (HF D1 and AISI Sol D5) rest on sources the AI coder could not read. HF D1 rests on R01, which returned HTTP 403 and was not re-verified, so it rests on a prior reading only. The 'not reauthenticated' status means it cannot be traced to a source anchor as the brief requires.

The built PDF has 7 main-text pages against a 6-page limit. The submission also refers throughout to repository files (experiments/data/..., n_refs_counts.json, number_ledger.csv, 'round 1/4/5') that a double-blind reviewer cannot access. The text is not anonymized in these respects, and the methods section is heavy with internal process detail.

Novelty is incremental, which the automated novelty check confirms. Cross-organization incident comparison overlaps with Raftari, Bouke and Amundsen, and the closest-work discussion originally omitted them. The 'claim-support matrix' is a 4×5 table of generic descriptions, and the O/A/I/X classes are not shown to add analytic value beyond ordinary provenance tagging. The X column has zero coded decisions, so it is empty in practice.

The numerical audit is thin. It reports 37 ledger rows and 30 anchors found, and it covers only anchors in cached sources. Row N42 (5.5% resampling) was added after the audit and is reported separately. Opus 4.7 resampling values were read from HTML alt text. The anchor checks use regex hit counts (e.g. 184 hits for 'message board') that show a keyword is present but not that the proposition is supported. Several figures (141,006 runs; 122 runs; 10 runs) rely on secondary extraction.

Several sources are cited by 'accessed' status that conflicts across records. R06 is listed as reopened in the ledger but as HTTP 429 in the findings. R31 is listed as opened in the ledger but as not opened in the findings. Many ledger entries (R36–R44) are 'scout summary only' sources, including low-quality commercial blogs. They pad the source inventory of 44 without supporting any finding.

Some claims about stage-level detection go beyond what the sources support. D4 is coded 'documented' for cells where the source reports only an observation (OpenAI May) or a failed abort (Opus 4.6). This stretches the 'documented' definition, and the interpretation of RQ3 relies on it. The RQ2 claim that the evidence separates recognizing reality from believing the action is authorized rests mainly on one developer's narrated account of its own model.
strengths: The paper is candid about its limits. It states the κ failure, the AI-only second coding, the single human coder, the uninformative bootstrap CI and the conflicting disagreement records. It does not overclaim validity.

The conceptual separations are useful. Reachability is kept apart from authorization, recognizing a real target from belief in permission, detection from intervention, and replay from live response. The paper keeps denominators distinct (122 runs, 19 actions, 5 datasets and 15 installations are not pooled).

The coding is traceable, with a per-cell evidence class, anchor IDs, a change log and a claim-strength downgrade log. The three agreeing cells are clearly marked. The disclosure checklist is concrete and practical for evaluators.
The documentary design involves no offensive experiments and adds no operational detail. Its scope claims are modest.

Section III-A describes selection through substantive documentation and contrasting conditions but gives no operational inclusion threshold or systematic candidate-identification procedure. The selected corpus therefore cannot be reconstructed from the stated selection rules alone.
The AI coding exercise lacks an exact model version, coding prompt, inference settings and complete second-coder output in the supplied material, limiting reproduction of the reported agreement.

The supplied evidence_class_rows.csv labels investigator interpretations and even unknown cells as direct evidence. This uniform directness coding does not implement the distinctions between directness and investigator inference emphasized in Section III-C.
strengths: The row-level matrix and complete 45-decision appendix provide a concrete, inspectable methodological increment beyond narrative incident comparison.
The analysis carefully separates technical access, perceived authorization, external actions, response stages and established effects.
Replay findings are attributed to their original investigators and are not presented as measurements of live intervention or production-defense efficacy.
The manuscript explicitly discloses source dependence, unavailable source text, unresolved disagreements and the failed reliability threshold.
The comparison addresses questions directly relevant to agent-security evaluators while avoiding prevalence estimates and unsupported causal claims.

A row-level, source-anchored claim-support matrix separating authorization belief, action, response and verified effects provides a clear, checkable methodological increment. The supplied summaries do not establish that listed work already provides this artifact.
